svg.title: How money moves through the trust account

g.text: Every entry is one of four kinds; its circled number is the step that made it
Cash · money in the trust account
Outside AA: the payers who pay in, and the anaesthetists' own bank accounts
Holds each procedure and raises its invoice first, then
submits it to Xero. Its ledger mirrors Xero, and must equal it.
AA's trust accounting, the dotted box on Greg's whiteboard.
Each T-account: debits on the left, credits on the right.
AA's one real bank account. Every receipt lands
here; every payout and refund leaves from here.
Accounts receivable. A control account: only
Accounts payable. A control account: only
Which entry is the buyer-created tax invoice, and
whether there is one per procedure or one per
A creditor beside the anaesthetists, "a fake anaesthetist": it
receives and transfers, but is never paid itself. Not a bank
account and not a ledger account. Money leaves it only through
Each sub-ledger must equal its control account, and
our ledger must equal Xero. If they don't balance, stop.
AA owes Dr Nick only once Patient 1 has paid:
"we never owe this until this is paid".
Prepayment invoice approved in our system
Drawn as on the whiteboard: this payable is recorded when the
money comes in. The catalogue creates it with the prepayment
invoice, at step 7 (OQ-80). To confirm with Greg.
A journal move between two creditors, not a payment or a new
invoice; nothing moves in the trust account. What releases it
once the procedure is done is still open (OQ-125).
The payment cycle is still to confirm with AA's

svg.text: Every dollar in the trust account is owed to someone: each sub-ledger equals its control account, and our ledger equals Xero
